# Pull Request

## Related issue
Fixes https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/issues/4432
Fixes https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/issues/4438 by adding the logs the user asked

## What does this PR do?
- Adds a bunch of logs to help debug this kind of issue in the future
- Delete the update files AFTER committing the update in the `index-scheduler` (thus, if a restart happens, we are able to re-process the batch successfully)
- Multi-thread the deletion of all update files.

issue_context.title: Make the processing of batches atomic
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
Currently, when meilisearch processes the tasks, there is three phases:
1. Find the tasks you need to process in your batch
2. Actually, process the batch, for example, index documents
3. Write the results in the task queue and delete the associated update files.

We just realized that there was a bug in step 3️⃣:
4. We take a write transaction on the task store
5. Loop over all the processed tasks
6. For each task: Write its new status and delete its associated update file
7. Commit the content of the task store

Here, if a crash/restart happens during the loop of 6️⃣, Meilisearch will restart, recreate a batch that contains at least the same tasks, and in step 2️⃣ realize that some of the update files have been deleted.
=> We just lost some data.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Index a ton of thing
2. Restart meilisearch in the middle of step 6️⃣ 


**Expected behavior**
We don't lose any tasks

**Meilisearch version:**
Everything above and including v0.30.0

review_comments: it would be better to create the read txn once (using the appropriate feature). Opening a lot of transactions in parallel can be slower than using the same one on different threads. What do you think?

How would I do that? By using the `sync-read-txn` heed feature?

Because yeah, I wasn’t happy about this solution, I thought of using [`for_each_init`](https://docs.rs/rayon/latest/rayon/iter/trait.ParallelIterator.html#method.for_each_init) with this code:
```rust
...
        ids.into_par_iter().try_for_each_init(
            || self.read_txn(),
            |rtxn, id| -> Result<()> {
                // let rtxn = self.read_txn();
                let rtxn = rtxn.as_ref().unwrap(); // here I can't `?` because I have a ref of error
                let task = self
                    .get_task(rtxn, id)
...
```
But from what I understand, it pretty much ends up calling my closure for every rayon job (thus every iteration, right?).

The other easy idea could be to split up the roaring bitmap into as many parts as we have threads and then let each thread open **one** `rtxn` and delete the batch of files on his side.
That’s probably better, but if one finishes early, the other will be waiting.

We could maybe fix that with an AtomicU64 + the `.select` method on the roaring bitmap as we did in Arroy. That seems a bit overkill, but tbh, it’s not that complex to write, and it works.

But let me know if you have anything else in mind
I implemented the last solution in https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/pull/4435/commits/066a7a3cde2695e7bd8c5d7460e1b500125d9647
